speaker: gauge
text: This train track sits on a pile of rocks. Messy. I'll lay it on plain dirt.

speaker: fitz
text:
Dirt won't hold. Trains are heavy, and wet dirt turns soft.
So railways use crushed stone, called ballast. It spreads the weight and lets rain drain through.

speaker: fitz
text: Sharp edges lock together and hold the ties in place. Round pebbles would roll.

speaker: fitz
text: Some lines do. Slab track costs more to build, but needs less fixing.

speaker: gauge
text: Ooh, what else is built weird? Subscribe and let's find out.
